summary: The Season Two prologue of Sirah Impak Sosial, given at the start of 2025. Ustaz Azlan explains the division of the sirah into three seasons and shares observations from his travels in the UAE, Qatar, the UK and the United States, then uses the couple Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and Asma' bint Umays as a doorway to see the effect of revelation. He describes the first migration to Abyssinia, the attempt by Amr ibn Al-As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah to persuade the Negus, Ja'far's speech that sums up Islam in under five minutes, the recitation of Surah Maryam that moved the Negus, and the end of Ja'far's life as a martyr at Mu'tah and the fate of his family.
keyPoints: The sirah is divided into three seasons: birth to age 40, the call in Makkah (ages 40 to 53), and Madinah until the Prophet's death.
The Prophet SAW sent his best companions to Abyssinia as a backup base, not because they were weak.
Quraysh sent Amr ibn Al-As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah with lavish gifts to persuade the Negus to return the Muslims.
Ja'far's speech moved from the problem of jahiliyyah to the change revelation brought and ended with a request for protection.
The recitation of Surah Maryam moved the Negus to tears and he rejected Quraysh's case.
Ja'far was separated from the Prophet SAW for 15 years, returned to Madinah when Khaybar was conquered, and was martyred at Mu'tah.
The story invites us to be like Ja'far and Asma', who were totally changed by revelation.

lessons.title: Appreciate Malaysia's food
lessons.body: The ustaz reminds us we waste a great deal of food although spices were once extremely costly.

lessons.title: Migration is not weakness
lessons.body: The companions sent to Abyssinia were the best, as a backup base.

lessons.title: Listen before judging
lessons.body: The Negus refused to decide before hearing the accused.

lessons.title: Mutual prejudice is jahiliyyah
lessons.body: Muslims and non-Muslims should not live in stereotypes about each other.

lessons.title: Learn to lobby and shape narratives
lessons.body: Young Muslims are needed in journalism, film and media because narratives shape how people think.

lessons.title: Present Islam in a short time
lessons.body: Ja'far began with the problem, the change and a request for protection, and left curiosity behind.

lessons.title: Do not compromise on belief
lessons.body: Ja'far called Jesus a servant and messenger of Allah without compromise despite the tension.

lessons.title: The Quran touches hearts
lessons.body: The Quran is an auditory experience that can capture hearts; get used to hearing its recitation.

lessons.title: Be confident in what we have
lessons.body: We often feel inferior and pay dearly for the same idea when it comes from a foreigner.

lessons.title: Keep family ties
lessons.body: Family is the greatest test, and true kinship comes from the same womb.

lessons.title: Help the bereaved
lessons.body: Bring food to a grieving family as the Prophet SAW told people to do for Ja'far's family.

lessons.title: The power of storytelling
lessons.body: A third of the Quran is stories; those who tell stories well shape narratives.

dalil.context: Exegetes say this verse refers to the Negus and the clergy who wept on hearing the Quran.
dalil.translation: and when they listen to what has been sent down to the Messenger, you will see their eyes overflowing with tears because they recognize the Truth [in it]. They say, ‘Our Lord, we believe, so count us amongst the witnesses.

dalil.context: Ja'far recited the start of Surah Maryam up to the birth of Jesus before the Negus. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
Scholars regard this as the best speech summing up Islam in under five minutes.
dalil.translation: O king, we were a jahili people who worshipped idols, ate carrion, committed indecencies, cut kinship ties and harmed neighbours; the strong devoured the weak, until Allah sent a messenger whose lineage, truthfulness and trustworthiness we knew.

dalil.context: Mentioned to stress how great keeping family ties is.
dalil.translation: Whoever cuts the ties of kinship, Allah will cut him off from His mercy.

dalil.context: The Prophet SAW chose Ja'far to raise Hamza's daughter because his wife Asma' was the girl's maternal aunt.
dalil.translation: A maternal aunt stands in the position of a mother.

dalil.context: The Prophet SAW comforted Asma' after telling her of Ja'far's martyrdom.
dalil.translation: I saw Ja'far in Paradise, given two wings and flying with the angels.
